transcript:
00:00 Alex Moreno: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, im alex from redwood inference, i'll be your AE for this onramp  
00:07 Priya Kapoor: hi all priya here, i'll do the SDK walk and the optimize demo, se on the call 
00:12 Samir Patel: great thanks alex priya, samir here, head of platform at lighthouse, dana and marcos from infra/security with me 
00:18 Dana Lee: hey 
00:19 Marcos Ruiz: morning all 
00:22 Alex Moreno: quick agenda — 1) run through python and typescript quickstarts 2) auth patterns (api keys vs sso + rotation) 3) sandbox vpc + kms notes 4) optimize tips for latency/cost 5) Qs and next steps, sound good? 
00:34 Samir Patel: yep that's perfect we're mainly trying to validate integration path and how much work to get into a sandbox, also curious about dedicated capacity numbers vs hosted pricing 
00:43 Priya Kapoor: cool i'll start with local quickstart, i'll share my screen (link: https://redwood.ai/sandbox-playbook) 
00:50 Priya Kapoor: ok so python quickstart — pip install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY or use our sso flow, here's a sample snippet 
00:58 Priya Kapoor: we often see teams do env var for dev and sso for prod, and rotate keys once a month as a minimum, but use KMS for extra safety 
01:10 Dana Lee: small Q — can the sdk pick up creds from aws parameter store / secrets manager automatically? 
01:15 Priya Kapoor: yep you can point the SDK to a token provider, there is a small adapter we ship, pr example in the repo — i'll put the link in the notes. it reads from aws secrets or from file, so common patterns are supported but you'll need to wire the role permissions on the instance. 
01:31 Samir Patel: how bad is the auth overhead for each request? we can't afford high handshake latency per token exchange per request 
01:37 Priya Kapoor: good call, auth is cached for short-lived tokens, so usually the per-request overhead is negligible — if you do sso you mint a session token and the SDK caches it, for api key it's a simple bearer header. we recommend long lived ephemeral tokens for high qps, and rotate out-of-band. 
01:50 Marcos Ruiz: from security we want audit logs, key rotation policy, and bring-your-own-kms (BYOK) support, are those available? 
01:58 Alex Moreno: yes SOC 2 and audit logs are in hosted, and for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM, and you can ship audit logs to your SIEM. i'll attach our security whitepaper after this call. 
02:09 Marcos Ruiz: ok good, also need to know data residency options — eu region specifically 
02:14 Priya Kapoor: region routing is policy-driven — you can pin requests to eu models and eu clusters, for private we can deploy into customer's VPC in a supported region. 
02:24 Dana Lee: walkthrough on typescript? we do node services mostly 
02:27 Priya Kapoor: sure, typescript quickstart is similar, npm i @redwood/sdk, then import RedwoodClient from '@redwood/sdk', set REDWOOD_API_KEY or use the web oauth flow. here's a tiny example using streaming responses for chat. 
02:41 Priya Kapoor: (flips to code) sample: const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'eu-west-1'}); await client.chat.stream(...). note that streaming uses a websocket under the hood, so ensure the service supports outbound ws. 
02:55 Samir Patel: nice — what's the usual deployment pattern for our infra team? do we run it inside our pods or call hosted endpoints? 
03:03 Alex Moreno: both are standard — many start with hosted to iterate then move to Dedicated or Private for isolation and predictable SLO. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and an SLA; Private gives VPC, KMS, on-prem if needed. 
03:15 Samir Patel: can you give a back-of-envelope of Dedicated vs Hosted cost per 1M tokens? we need ballpark for budget 
03:21 Alex Moreno: i'll send a TCO spreadsheet; rough numbers: hosted variable per-token with volume discounts, Dedicated is commit-based and usually lower unit cost at scale, i'll include examples in the spreadsheet specific to your expected QPS. 
03:33 Dana Lee: firewall and network setup — if we go with private can we terminate inside our vpc? 
03:38 Priya Kapoor: yes Private control plane is customer-managed and data egress can be kept internal, we hand off a terraform module that provisions the gateway into your vpc, and we support mutual TLS for service-to-service. 
03:51 Marcos Ruiz: any quantization or model variants we should consider? we have latency-sensitive use cases 
03:55 Priya Kapoor: good one — for low-latency we recommend optimized fp16 or int8 variants where applicable; Optimize will suggest quantization profiles based on your workload; note there is a slight inference-quality delta sometimes, we recommend running evals against your prompt set. 
04:12 Samir Patel: about Optimize — can it auto-suggest batching parameters? we saw the mention of continuous batching in the docs 
04:18 Priya Kapoor: yes, Optimize provides workload-aware batching suggestions, it looks at sequence length distribution and latency SLOs, and recommends batch sizes and batching windows. also the runtime does automatic prefix caching and kv cache to speed up chat scenarios. 
04:33 Alex Moreno: i'm going to demo a simple end-to-end: typescript service calling Redwood hosted, then switch to a local sandbox demo that mimics Private. priya will run the optimize console for a short example. 
04:45 Priya Kapoor: switching to the console — (screen share) this is the per-route dashboard, you can see token cost, p95 latency, and there's an 'optimize' tab that recommends batch windows. here's a sample recommendation for a support-chat flow — increase batch window to 30ms and set batch size 8 to reduce cost by 22% while keeping p95 under 250ms. 
05:10 Dana Lee: that recommendation assumes some patience for first token right? how does it affect cold starts? 
05:15 Priya Kapoor: yes micro-batching trades off first-token latency vs throughput; the console shows a slider so you can dial to your SLO. for cold starts we have warmers and reserved pools in Dedicated to avoid cold-starts. 
05:28 Samir Patel: can we run benchmarks in your sandbox and collect logs to our prometheus? we want to compare with our benchmarks for the gateway 
05:34 Alex Moreno: absolutely — the sandbox hands you an endpoint and we can forward metrics to your prometheus/grafana via exporters, or you can pull traces from our tracing hooks. 
05:45 Marcos Ruiz: any limitations on request size or token limits when running on sandbox? 
05:49 Priya Kapoor: sandbox mirrors hosted limits for token length; for Private/Dedicated we can tune sequence length and kernels per your workload but it'll be part of onboarding. 
05:59 Samir Patel: ok let's talk about the quickstart steps we need to follow this week, we want to get a dev sandbox and run an initial 10k token test by next week 
06:07 Alex Moreno: plan: 1) we provision a sandbox account and you get a short-lived api key 2) priya shares terraform and quickstart scripts 3) you run the throughput test 4) we review results and pick Dedicated vs Hosted pilot — i'll capture these as next steps. 
06:18 Priya Kapoor: i'll paste the quickstart repo link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/tree/main/sandbox-js-py and a terraform module: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/tree/main/sandbox-vpc. those both have example env and secret wiring. 
06:32 Dana Lee: thanks, i'll look at the terraform. a small note: our security team insists on BYOK for keys, is that supported in sandbox? 
06:40 Alex Moreno: sandbox uses managed KMS, but for Private deployments we support BYOK/HSM. for sandbox we can also configure customer KMS in many cases if you provide the CMKs — we'll check that in the onboarding ticket. 
06:52 Marcos Ruiz: please share the SOC 2 report and any pen-test summaries 
06:55 Alex Moreno: yes i'll send the security pack, pen-test summary redacted for public but we can do an NDA if you need full details. 
07:04 Priya Kapoor: quick live demo: i'll run the python example — (typing) pip install redwood-sdk... setting REDWOOD_API_KEY, running sample generation. you might see a small transient on the first request while the runtime allocates, this is normal. 
07:20 Priya Kapoor: running now — sample customer support prompt — ok output looks good, tokens 320, latency 210ms p50, p95 480ms. 
07:33 Samir Patel: those latencies are in eu-west? 
07:36 Priya Kapoor: this sandbox cluster is in us-west but pinning to eu-west would increase p95 slightly, typically 10-20% with cross-region egress — we'll mirror in eu during your sandbox if needed. 
07:49 Dana Lee: what about SDK error handling patterns — retries, idempotency? we need to ensure dedup on our side 
07:55 Priya Kapoor: SDK exposes retry policies and you can plug in your own idempotency keys; for streaming we surface partial transcripts and an ack model so you can replay from kv-cache if needed. 
08:07 Samir Patel: are there any gotchas for node serverless lambdas and ephemeral containers? 
08:12 Priya Kapoor: yes cold-starts are more pronounced in serverless — use the streaming websocket and keep a warm connection pool, or use Dedicated reserved capacity to avoid cold starts. we'll include a serverless example in the repo. 
08:26 Alex Moreno: quick pause for questions? 
08:28 Marcos Ruiz: wondering about compliance with EU data residency and audit logs — we'll need logs shipped to our SIEM and not stored beyond retention policy 
08:36 Alex Moreno: logging retention is configurable, hosted can forward logs and redact content; Private is fully under your control. we'll share the retention and SIEM integration guide. 
08:47 Priya Kapoor: last piece — Optimize has a regression alerting feature where you can tie eval prompt sets; if model quality drops the platform alerts and can auto-fallback to a previous model variant. great for production safety. 
08:58 Samir Patel: excellent, that helps. timeline wise we want to choose pilot by Sept 12 if the sandbox results look good, is that feasible? 
09:05 Alex Moreno: yes that fits — our tickets: provision sandbox (1-2 days), run tests (3-5 days), review. i'll mark the pilot decision target Sept 12. 
09:15 Dana Lee: any competitor comparisons in the security docs? marcos asked about differences vs anthro/openai 
09:21 Alex Moreno: we'll include a short competitor appendix comparing hosted features, pricing model, and private deployment support; high level: many peers offer hosted endpoints, fewer offer the unified private+dedicated runtime and first-class optimize tooling. 
09:36 Priya Kapoor: ok wrapping up, i'll follow-up in the calendar with links and the quickstart repo. alex will send pricing and security docs. can we recap next steps? 
09:45 Alex Moreno: recap: Alex send pricing + SOC2 + security pack + competitor appendix by 2025-09-03; Priya send sandbox terraform + quickstart scripts by 2025-09-05; Lighthouse to run initial 10k token throughput test and provide prompt telemetry by 2025-09-04; schedule benchmark review call week of 2025-09-08 — does that look right? 
09:59 Samir Patel: yep that's good, thanks everyone 
10:02 Marcos Ruiz: thanks, appreciate it 
10:04 Dana Lee: thanks, talk soon 
10:06 Alex Moreno: thanks all, i'll send notes and the links — bye 
10:10 (call ends)
